title: Pacing bench
intro: Change the producer counts, outputs and curves in the settings. The pacing simulator re-runs in your browser and shows when each player profile reaches each step. Dashed lines and small numbers compare against the pinned reference.

fields.producersPerTowerHint: one of each starting type per tower
fields.producersAhead: Producer levels ahead of the Longhouse
fields.productionGrowthHint: each level adds ×this more than the last
fields.costGrowthHint: all standard types, not the Longhouse or storage

status.pinned: Pinned the current run as the reference
status.copyBlocked: Copy is blocked here; the settings are selected in the field below
status.error: The simulator stopped with an error: {message}

milestones.title: When each profile gets there
milestones.note: Day reached (day 0 = founding at 09:00). Small numbers: change in days against the reference. Red: later, green: sooner.

how.title: What the profiles mean
how.active: Online every day from {from} to {to} and acts the moment a build slot is free. Offline {offlineHours} hours at night, when nothing new starts but running builds finish.
how.checkins4: Four short visits a day, at {times}. A check-in is a {minutes}-minute session: the player fills every free slot and starts a feast if one can run, then logs off until the next visit.
how.feasts: A feast at the Town Square costs {cost} × {costGrowth}^(TS−1) each of wood, brick and food, runs {hours} hours and then grants {renown} × {renownGrowth}^(TS−1) renown (TS is the Town Square level). One feast at a time per settlement, no build slot used. “No feasts” earns renown only from buildings.
how.renown: +1 per standing building level per hour, never spent. The 2nd settlement needs the renown threshold (settings), a Cart Workshop ({prerequisite}, paid for like any building) and the five Settlers’ cost in stock.
how.day0: The player founds the settlement at {time} with {wood} wood, {stone} brick and {food} food and no iron.
how.decides: How the simulated player decides: it keeps its starting producers at most “levels ahead” above the Longhouse and upgrades the Longhouse once they have caught up. While it saves for the Longhouse it still upgrades a producer that pays back its cost before the Longhouse would be affordable. Each tower the Longhouse allows adds one more producer of each starting type, built after the starting set. Storage is built only when the next Longhouse level or producer level would not fit: the best capacity per cost among upgrading a Storage House, a new Storage House (only when none can be upgraded) and a Great Storehouse. No raids, no troops, no terrain boosts.

cost.title: Longhouse wood cost per level
cost.note: Brick costs 5/6 of the wood, food half of it. Levels 1–5 cost no brick. The reference value is in brackets.
